title: Pointwise Convergence of Random Ergodic Averages at the \(L^1\) Endpoint
summary: In his highly influential paper, \emph{On the maximal ergodic theorem for certain subsets of the integers}, Bourgain introduced the study of pointwise convergence of ergodic averages along randomly generated subsets of the integers, developing a robust \(L^p\)-theory for \(p>1\). More recently, this theory was partially complemented at the \(L^1\) endpoint by work of LaVictoire, who treated averages along random sequences that are ``slightly denser" than the set of squares, for which universal \(L^1\) pointwise convergence is known to fail.
